correctness.rationale: All orbit classes have a unique Hensel lift for the first mod-p hit of zero since the derivative of f^tau is a unit; the lift is a valuation isometry. The critical-cycle identity f²(y)=y²(y²−2) yields exact valuation doubling for odd p. The first-entry time and exceptional -1 lift are handled separately, shell coefficients are exact, and the claimed maximum is witnessed by s=1. The standalone direct-iteration checker verifies complete histograms in 43 finite cases, not claimed as a universal proof.

value.rationale: The theorem produces the complete first-entry time distribution of a natural critical-cycle basin across all odd-prime-power rings, with a closed factorized polynomial and O(log k) shell terms; it gives sharp maxima and distinguishes full attraction at p=3,7 from a proper basin at p=5. These are natural structural invariants and not arbitrary bounded computations.
